chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from 'Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The proud (al-jabbārūn) are the farthest of people from Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الْجَبَّارُونَ: The proud, the haughty, those who are domineering

ai.seo_question: Who is farthest from Allah on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this narration specifically identifies 'al-jabbārūn'—those who are not merely proud but actively domineering and oppressive over others—as the furthest from Allah. This distinction aligns with the Shia exegetical tradition where *jabarūt* implies a forceful imposition of will, making it a more severe spiritual state than simple arrogance (*kibr*). The hadith serves as a potent eschatological warning, linking social oppression directly to ultimate divine distance.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 11. And from the previous chain from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from ’Amru b. Jamee’ from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
Proud people will be farthest from Allah on the Day of Judgment.”
